key_insight: AeroZoo shows that encoding boundary conditions sharply improves aerodynamic flow prediction, while unseen enclosures and boundary-condition layouts remain major generalization challenges.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests whether neural CFD surrogates can transfer across shapes, flow domains and operating conditions rather than interpolate within one design family.
method: Compile 3,815 time-mean unsteady RANS solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosures and Reynolds numbers from 10³ to 10⁸.
Specify each problem using boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values and fluid properties.
Evaluate two tasks with engineering metrics and 22 frozen, geometry-disjoint splits.
evidence_signal: On the 2,816-sample stable-mean benchmark, boundary-condition tokens reduced GeoTransolver’s random-split median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of inlet speed in single-seed runs; ISLA reached 5.3% over four seeds.
watch_item: ISLA’s error increased 2.4–9.2× on held-out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts, cautioning against assuming reliable transfer to new flow domains.
paper_title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
